overview:
Destination safety is a pure function of a URL and the operator's denylist, placed beside the existing URL rules. It runs in two places: when a link is created, and when a stored link is resolved for a redirect, which is how existing links are covered without touching their rows.

Device analytics extends the existing click path by one value. The redirect route reduces the User-Agent header to a device class and hands the class, not the header, to the click recorder. The class is stored with the click event and aggregated by the statistics service.

components.name: Host rules
components.responsibility: Internal-host detection, denylist matching, denylist parsing. No I/O.

components.name: URL policy
components.responsibility: Apply the host rules on create, and expose the re-check used on redirect.

components.name: Configuration and wiring
components.responsibility: Read and validate DENIED_HOSTS; pass it to the link service.

components.name: Link service
components.responsibility: Validate against the denylist on create; block a disallowed stored destination on resolve.

components.name: Device classification
components.responsibility: Map a User-Agent header to one of five classes.

components.name: Click path
components.responsibility: Classify at the route, store the class with the event, aggregate by class.

apiChanges.change: Destinations on internal or denied hosts now return 400.

dataModelChanges: click_events.device_class TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown', constrained to desktop, mobile, tablet, bot, unknown.

decisions.title: Judge a destination by its text, without resolving DNS
decisions.decision: Parse the URL and test its host: address literals against the non-public ranges, names against localhost, single-label and internal suffixes, and the operator's denylist. No DNS lookup is made.
decisions.rationale: The standard URL parser already turns disguised forms such as 2130706433 or 0x7f.1 into a dotted address, so a text check catches them. A DNS lookup would put a network call driven by user input on both the create and the redirect path, and the answer can change between the check and the visit.
alternatives: Resolve the name and check the addresses: catches public names pointing at private addresses, at the cost of latency, a network dependency and a time-of-check gap
Call a reputation service: an external dependency, and it sends every submitted URL to a third party

decisions.title: Re-check the destination on every redirect
decisions.decision: LinkService.resolve applies the same rules to the stored URL that create applies to a new one.
decisions.rationale: The requester confirmed that existing links must be covered. Checking at redirect time means a denylist change takes effect immediately for every link, with no migration or batch job, and it costs one URL parse on a row already loaded.
alternatives: A one-off job that marks existing links as blocked: has to be re-run on every denylist change, and adds state that can go stale
Check only on create: leaves every existing unsafe link live

decisions.title: A blocked link answers 410 with link_blocked and reveals nothing
decisions.decision: Return 410 as a problem document with code link_blocked, no Location header, and a message that does not contain the destination.
decisions.rationale: It matches how an expired link is reported, so clients handle one more code rather than a new mechanism. Withholding the destination avoids advertising the unsafe URL.
alternatives: An interstitial warning page with a continue button: still delivers people to the destination
404: hides from the owner that the link was blocked rather than lost

decisions.title: Store a coarse device class, never the User-Agent
decisions.decision: Classify the header in memory at the redirect route into one of five classes and store only that class with the click.
decisions.rationale: The requester confirmed that nothing identifying a visitor may be stored. A raw User-Agent, especially combined with a timestamp and a referrer, can single out a person; one of five class names cannot.
alternatives: Store the header and classify when reporting: flexible, but holds personal data
Store a hash of address and User-Agent to count unique visitors: a persistent visitor identifier, ruled out by Q-1

decisions.title: Classify with a small set of patterns in-process
decisions.decision: A handful of regular expressions over the first 512 characters of the header, with bots tested first.
decisions.rationale: Five coarse classes do not need a device database. No new dependency enters the build, and bounding the inspected length bounds the cost of an oversized header.
alternatives: A User-Agent parsing library: more accurate for browser and OS detail nobody asked for, and a new dependency to approve and keep patched

risks.risk: A public host name that resolves to a private address is not detected.
risks.mitigation: Accepted and documented under ADR-1. The service never fetches the destination itself, so this is not a server-side request forgery path; the exposure is a visitor inside a network being sent to an internal address.

risks.risk: The denylist is only as good as its maintenance.
risks.mitigation: Documented as a first measure. A reputation feed is a recorded follow-up.

risks.risk: An over-broad denylist entry blocks legitimate links, including existing ones, immediately.
risks.mitigation: Entries are validated as host names at startup; matching is by host and subdomain only, never by substring. Removing the entry restores the links at once because nothing is stored.

risks.risk: Device classes are heuristic: a bot that sends a browser's User-Agent is counted as that browser, and recent iPads identify as desktop.
risks.mitigation: Documented. The class named bot is defined as clients that identify themselves as automated.

risks.risk: Adding a constrained not-null column validates existing click_events rows during the migration.
risks.mitigation: The default satisfies the constraint for every row. On a very large table the migration should be run in a maintenance window.

risks.risk: Creation requests that used to succeed are now rejected.
risks.mitigation: This is the intent of the change. The error message states that the destination is not allowed.

requirementCoverage.how: normalizeTargetUrl rejects a destination whose host isInternalHost reports as internal.
The same function rejects a host that isDeniedHost matches against the configured list; parseDeniedHosts validates the setting at startup.
LinkService.resolve calls isAllowedDestination on the stored URL and raises link_blocked before any click is queued.
The redirect route calls classifyDevice, the recorder stores the class, and StatsService groups click_events by it and reports every class.
